messages:
alex: RFC follow-up: proposal for temporary mapped-window leases for staged host pages to cut tail-latency for mixed streaming + batch inference. idea: instead of full migration or repeated host fetches, we allocate a short-lived GPU residency window (N ms, X pages) tied to the microbatch. lease is preemptible on pressure, and we expose per-endpoint hints so interactive traffic gets preferential lease sizing. want quick take on tradeoffs + implement concerns.

michael: short qs — how do we pick N and X in practice? how is this different than existing staging/prefetch? also worried about added fragmentation.

sara: seems like a soft-pin + timebox. two immediate concerns: (1) hole/pin fragmentation if many short leases land on adjacent addr ranges, (2) fairness across tenants. tie leases to kvcache prefix + request priority. fallback plan: if preempted, tiny-batch requeue to avoid large latency spike.

devon: NUMA/copy-cost is a legit worry — if host mapping lives on remote node, we pay cross-node DMA + PCIe hop. need affinity hints or prefer allocs from local node. also how do we surface the unit cost (for telemetry/billing)?

alex: answers + sketch: pick N ~ 50–200ms for streaming tail cases (tunable), X based on typical seq-length working set (e.g., 32–256 pages). difference from prefetch: prefetch is speculative and happens ahead of request; lease is reactive and guarantees short residency for imminent token generation without doing a heavyweight migration/compaction. it reduces fetch spikes by giving a small, preemptible landing zone. sample config we can surface in endpoint config: 

```json
{
  "lease_window_pages": 64,
  "lease_duration_ms": 150,
  "preempt_policy": "LRU_DEMOTE",
  "priority_tier_hint": "interactive",
  "numa_affinity": "auto"
}
```

we'd map lease tokens into the allocator header and expose a runtime path for preempt/revoke.

michael: concrete implement flow? proposer: allocator grants lease -> runtime pins pages and attaches token -> request executes -> if pressure, an async revoke RPC marks token revoked -> request runtime checks token on next safe point and triggers demote or spill. need robust cleanup on revoke.

sara: let's ensure we collect these metrics before/after experiment: lease_success_rate, lease_revoke_rate, tail_latency_p95/p99, pinned_pages_per_tenant, remap_cross_numa_ratio. use existing trace-replay harness to simulate bursty streaming + batch combos.

devon: plus: coalescing to reduce fragmentation — round leases to 4KiB granularity and try buddy-coalesce adjacent leases on free. fairness: add tenant soft-quotas for lease_pages; when exceeded, mark requests as "no-lease" and fall back to existing paths.

ci-bot: deploy-bench: lease-experiment branch failed mem-leak-check on macrotask 42. pinned-pages not freed after preempt. log: https://ci.fake/reports/lease-experiment/42 (short)

alex: ack, thanks @ci-bot. will add explicit revoke cleanup + unit test. plan: feature-flag behind "lease_window" experiment; run perf traces, gather metrics, and iterate. drafting RFC PR with diagrams + latency plots from replay. volunteers for POC? tagging: @michael @sara @devon

michael: I can take allocator changes + token revoke path (p2).

sara: I'll own telemetry, replay harness, and perf dashboards.

devon: I'll handle NUMA affinity logic, cross-node copy sim, and fairness policy.

alex: :thumbsup: great. I'll write the RFC PR and a short explainer doc with fallback semantics. expected next steps: POC branch, perf replay, RFC review, then canary on dedicated pool.

sara: one more thought — consider a hybrid: if a tenant repeatedly gets revoked > threshold, runtime should propose a model-variant fallback (smaller k-v cache quantized) to avoid constant churn.

alex: yeah good call — include model-variant fallback hook in the rollout policy.

michael: noted. will add a TODO in the allocator PR for model-variant hook.

devon: also add a stress test that simulates random lease revokes and cross-nvlink copies.

alex: thanks all — I'll open the PR by EOD with a POC branch and the initial config schema.
